note_text:
Patient presents to clinic requesting "a full allergy panel" after seeing an advertisement online for comprehensive allergen testing. Patient denies any specific symptoms such as rhinitis, urticaria, wheezing, or anaphylaxis. No history of asthma, eczema, or prior allergic reactions to foods, drugs, or environmental exposures. Review of systems is entirely negative for respiratory, dermatologic, or GI complaints. Physical exam was not performed at this visit; patient was seen briefly at the front desk and vitals were not obtained. No documentation of nasal mucosa, skin, or lung exam findings.

Given patient's request, ordered RAST panel for multiple environmental antigens (tree pollen, grass, mold, dust mite, cat/dog dander) and food antigens (egg, milk, peanut, soy) simultaneously to "screen for anything he might be allergic to." No specific clinical indication or exposure history was elicited to justify selection of these particular antigens; testing was ordered purely at patient's request without a preceding history and physical to identify suspected triggers.

Plan: Await RAST results, will discuss further management once results are back. Follow up in 2 weeks.
